title: First-Hour Stabilization SOP and Executive Incident Brief
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

Purpose: This document codifies a repeatable, auditable first-hour stabilization SOP for operator teams (SRE, serving runtime, product support) and provides a template executive incident brief. The goal is to restore customer-visible service levels quickly, gather forensic evidence, and produce an actionable post-incident plan.

Audience: SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, support leads, and engineering managers.

Scope: Applies to production inference service incidents impacting latency SLOs, error-rate regressions, large-scale capacity failures (regional or multi-tenant), and model-quality degradations that require cross-team coordination. Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks but provides a universal first-hour ladder and comms templates.

Quick reference:
- Severity mapping: P0 (system-wide outage), P1 (SLO breach impacting many tenants), P2 (single-customer impact or degraded quality), P3 (minor/non-customer-facing degradations).
- Primary contact channel: #ops-bridge Slack channel and incident Zoom bridge (automatically created by pager).
- Required immediate outputs in first 60 minutes: triage summary, mitigation action(s) in flight, customer-visible status published, executive brief stub created.

Roles & responsibilities:

- Incident Commander (IC): Owns coordination, decisions, and the executive brief. Typical IC rotation: senior SRE on-call.
- Service Steward: Owner of the impacted service (e.g., serving-runtime lead). Responsible for technical diagnosis and runbook execution.
- Bridge Operator: Manages comms, runbook links, status page updates.
- Escalation Engineer: SME (runtime/kernel/model) pulled for deep technical fixes.
- Customer Liaison (for P1/P0): Support/CS rep for customer notifications and impact assessment.

Severity decision ladder (short):
1) Confirm alert signal (AlertName, count, query) and scope (region, model, tenant).
2) Check SLO dashboards: 99th latency, error-rate, request-success ratio for the last 5m and 1h.
3) If ≥ 50% of global requests show SLO violation OR > 3 enterprise customers affected -> escalate to P0/P1.
4) If single-customer only AND mitigations exist (route/disable) -> P2.

First-hour stabilization checklist (step-by-step, numbered):

1. Acknowledge and declare incident (0-2 minutes)
   - IC acknowledges pager, moves to #ops-bridge, and posts initial one-line incident declaration: "Investigating elevated 99p latency for text-generation (region: us-west-2)."
   - Bridge operator documents alert name, originating alert rule, pager time, and initial SIG (SLO/availability/quality).

2. Rapid scope & safety checks (2-8 minutes)
   - Validate whether the alert is synthetic or real (look for matching synthetic failures).
   - Confirm telemetry: traces, sample error logs, and load metrics (RPS, queue length, GPU util, KV cache hit rate).
   - If throttling/backpressure is present, enable pre-approved escape hatch (eg: bump per-customer concurrency limits for critical customers).

3. Apply immediate mitigations (8-20 minutes)
   - Hotfix options (choose the least invasive first): 1) Route traffic to warm standby region; 2) Scale dedicated pool for high-impact customers; 3) Roll back recent model/config rollout; 4) Engage fallback model variant (quantized/cheaper).
   - Document chosen mitigation, operator, ETA for effect, and metrics to watch.

4. Contain & preserve evidence (20-35 minutes)
   - Freeze relevant autoscaling and deployment operations to prevent noisy artifacts.
   - Increase retention for traces/logs for impacted services for at least 72 hours (evidence TTL).
   - Snapshot key runtime state: KV cache eviction counts, model KV cache keys for affected sessions, and GPU kernel traces.

5. Customer & status communications (30-45 minutes)
   - Publish initial customer-facing status page entry (template below) and post a short note in the account-level status channels for affected enterprise customers.
   - If P0/P1, prepare an exec brief stub and circulate to leadership list (email + Slack).

6. Stabilize and handoff to long-running remediation (45-60 minutes)
   - If mitigation restores SLOs, build a rollback/cleanup plan and assign owners for full root-cause analysis (RCA).
   - If SLOs are not restored, escalate to extended incident (schedule additional escalation cadence and mobilize postmortem team).

Forensic evidence checklist (must be collected within first hour):
- SLO time series (1m/5m/1h) for latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate, and success ratio.
- Trace samples covering at least 100 failed/spike requests.
- GPU telemetry: GPU util, memory, kernel error counters, and process-level metrics.
- Autoscaler and scheduling events with timestamps.
- Recent deployments and model-rollout hashes (git commits, model version IDs).
- KV cache metrics: hit/miss/evict counts and notable prefix keys.
- Model-quality signals: eval-set regressions and recent production prompt-eval deltas (if available).

Escalation matrix & time targets:
- 0 minutes: Pager fired and primary on-call acknowledges.
- 5 minutes: IC declared if multiple signals confirmed.
- 15 minutes: Escalation engineer (runtime/model) paged for P0/P1.
- 30 minutes: CS Customer Liaison engaged for any enterprise-impacting incidents.

Communication templates:

1) Internal bridge headline (post on #ops-bridge):
   - Subject: [INCIDENT] One-line summary | SEV | region | impact
   - Body: Timestamp (UTC), IC name, short problem statement, primary mitigation in flight, immediate next-check (time).

Example: "[INCIDENT] P1: Elevated p99 latency for text-gen in us-west-2 — 2026-02-03T17:24Z — IC: Maya Chen — Routing traffic to warm standby region (eta 6m) — next check 17:30Z."

2) Customer-facing status page template (short):
   - Title: Service Degradation — Text Generation — us-west-2
   - Impact: Some requests are seeing increased latency (> p99 target of 450ms).
   - Start time: 2026-02-03T17:18Z UTC
   - What we're doing: Investigating root cause; routing traffic to alternative region and scaling affected pools.
   - Next update: 30 minutes

3) Executive incident brief stub (one page):
   - Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-####
   - Summary (3 lines): What happened, customer/system impact, high level mitigation.
   - Current status: Contains live metrics snapshot (p99, error-rate, capacity) and mitigation in-flight.
   - Owners: IC, Service Steward, Escalation SME, Customer Liaison.
   - Near-term actions (0-4h) and decision points.

Postmortem skeleton (to be completed after stabilization):
- Title and incident ID
- Timeline (minute-resolution, first hour and then key decision points)
- Impact summary (customers affected, SLO hours lost, credit calculations if any)
- Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence
- Corrective actions (short-term mitigations) and long-term fixes (owner + ETA)
- Learnings and follow-ups (owner + due date)
- Link to recorded bridge audio, logs, and forensic artifacts

Action item tracker format (table-like text you can paste into Tasks):
- [ ] Owner: Service Steward — Action: Harden autoscaler threshold to avoid oscillation — Due: 2026-02-10
- [ ] Owner: Runtime Eng — Action: Add KPI alert for KV cache evictions above 500/min — Due: 2026-02-17

Game-day and training plan (quarterly run):
- Focus: KV cache pressure + noisy neighbor + partial region degradations.
- Participants: On-call rotation, runtime engineers, product support, CS for customer-notice rehearsal.
- Duration: 3 hours with a 30-minute hotwash.
- Measurables: RTO (restore to SLO) target of < 60 minutes for simulated P1, evidence collection completeness > 90%.
- Exercise artifacts: synthetic load scripts, model-rollout simulation harness, and status page publishing exercise.

Runbook invocation & automation hooks (examples):
- Auto-runbook trigger: pager->bridge automation posts the incident template and populates the IC field.
- CLI snippet (example) to snapshot traces and increase retention:
   - rwi traces export --service serving-runtime --from now-30m --to now --out /tmp/incident-INC-XXXX.traces
   - rwi logs set-retention --service serving-runtime --minutes 4320

Service-level SLOs & thresholds (examples):
- Text-generation API: p99 latency target = 450ms; error-rate target = < 0.3% (1h window).
- Embeddings API: p99 latency target = 250ms; error-rate target = < 0.2%.
- Dedicated pools: tail latency SLO applies per-customer over 30m sliding window.

Operational hygiene & runbook governance:
- Every runbook invoked in an incident must have a runbook invocation note (who ran it, time, result).
- Runbooks reviewed quarterly; changes require owners to publish a summary of edits in the runbook changelog.
- Retire or consolidate runbooks after three consecutive failed-invocation tests in game-day exercises.

Appendix: Example evidence extraction checklist (copy/paste)
- [ ] Export 200 trace samples covering failed requests
- [ ] Capture autoscaler event log (last 60 minutes)
- [ ] Snapshot GPU /proc and kernel dmesg output
- [ ] Store model version artifact id and rollout config
- [ ] Collect sample prompts and model outputs for quality regressions

- Serving-runtime runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/serving-runtime-hotfixes-2025
- Incident comm templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- Status page docs and automation: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comm-automation-2025

Contact & escalation contact list (example placeholders):
- IC rotation (primary): oncall-sre@redwood.ai (PagerDuty)
- Runtime SME: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
- Model quality SME: model-quality@redwood.ai
- Executive distribution list: exec-ops@redwood.ai
